findings.problem: load_sensors fuses file I/O (fs::read_to_string), domain construction, and logging (println!) into a single function, violating Data/Calculations/Actions architecture. The shell and calculation layers are inseparable.
findings.failure_mode: Caller cannot reuse parsing logic without triggering disk I/O; tests cannot stub or mock the file read; pure property of the calculation is destroyed, making reasoning and verification impossible.
findings.fix: Split into two functions: a pure parse_sensors(lines: &[&str]) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> with no I/O or logging, and a shell load_sensors(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> that reads the file, handles I/O errors, and calls the pure parser.

findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() discards the fallible Result and panics on I/O failure (missing file, permission denied, too large).
findings.failure_mode: Entire process aborts on any I/O error with no recovery, no diagnostic context, and no typed error returned to the caller.
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and use map_err to convert io::Error into a typed LoadError::Io(e), propagating the error upward.

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is side-effecting I/O embedded in the parsing logic. Pure calculation must not produce stdout output.
findings.failure_mode: Parser output is contaminated with logging; pure function property is violated; output cannot be suppressed in tests without capturing stdout; logging is a shell concern, not a calculation concern.
findings.fix: Remove println! entirely from parse logic. Logging belongs in the shell layer after load_sensors returns. If observation is needed, return an opaque event or let the caller log.

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] use unchecked indexing into a Vec produced by split(','). Malformed lines with fewer than 2 fields will panic.
findings.failure_mode: A CSV line missing a comma or second field causes a panic at runtime instead of returning a typed ParseError.
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) to extract (_name, value_str), then parse value_str. Never index into split results.

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics when the second field is not a valid u32 (e.g., negative, non-numeric, empty, or overflow).
findings.failure_mode: Malformed numeric input aborts the process instead of yielding a typed ParseError::Invalid for the caller to handle.
findings.fix: Use .parse::<u32>().map_err(|_| ParseError::Invalid) and then checked conversion to u16 with u16::try_from(val).map_err(|_| ParseError::Invalid) or a domain-specific overflow error.

findings.problem: parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 is a lossy cast: any u32 value > 65535 silently truncates to u16 without error.
findings.failure_mode: Values 65536+ become 0, 65537 become 1, etc. Data corruption occurs silently with no diagnostic, violating bounded resources and explicit failure modes.
findings.fix: After parsing to u32, use u16::try_from(val).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow) to produce a typed overflow error for out-of-range values.

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(|part| part.trim().to_string()).collect() allocates a Vec<String> for every line, wasting memory and preventing use of split_once which is mandatory for one-separator grammars.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary allocation per line; the pattern prevents correct error handling for malformed lines; it also makes it easy to write parts[0]/parts[1] indexing which panics.
findings.fix: Use let (_name, value_str) = line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid)?; and parse value_str.trim() directly.

findings.problem: load_sensors returns Vec<Record> with no upper bound, no try_reserve, and no domain-cap validation. File length is unbounded, so a large file causes unbounded heap allocation.
findings.failure_mode: A sufficiently large file triggers OOM without graceful degradation; no allocation budget exists; the function has no domain cap on record count.
findings.fix: Add a max_items: usize parameter; validate it against a domain cap; create Vec::new(); call values.try_reserve(max_items).map_err(|_| ParseError::Allocation)?; enforce max_items before push; return Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>.

findings.problem: Record.name is pub name: String — a raw primitive with no domain invariants, validation, or newtype wrapper. Any caller can construct a Record with an invalid name.
findings.failure_mode: Illegal name values (empty, whitespace-only, containing commas) are representable and silently accepted, violating make-illegal-states-unrepresentable.
findings.fix: Introduce a named newtype SensorName(String) with a smart constructor that validates non-empty and no-commas, or use a typestate enum. Remove pub access from name field.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for the stated or implied performance characteristics of load_sensors
no profiler evidence to identify the actual bottleneck (I/O vs parsing vs allocation)
no allocation analysis (e.g., cargo-miri or alloc-deps) for unbounded Vec growth
no second-ring evidence for any performance or zero-cost claims
no command-line interface or command-truth evidence for the load_sensors functionality
no tests exist for the crate
no error taxonomy is defined (ParseError, LoadError types are absent)
residual_risk: Static review only with no commands run. The source contains 9 findings including 8 blockers: hidden I/O fused into calculation layer, two unwrap panic surfaces, unchecked indexing, lossy u32-to-u16 cast, split-collect instead of split_once, unbounded allocation with no try_reserve, and raw String domain state. All blockers require repair before any delivery gate passes. No benchmarks, tests, error types, or CLI evidence exist.
